fields.sample_size: approximately 1,000 households in four rural and four peri-urban water supply systems (Valle del Cauca, Colombia), randomly selected from water-bill or customer lists; one adult per household; plus participatory meetings with system managers
fields.study_design: cross-sectional household questionnaire survey with system-level water-supplied estimates and participatory meetings (mixed-methods case study)
fields.effect_estimate: Perceived household water use was statistically similar across the four rural systems and significantly lower than in the peri-urban systems; most rural systems had very low ratios of perceived use to water supplied, indicating conveyance losses or non-domestic use. Household size, education, age and occupation were the main factors; peri-urban users (younger, more educated) perceived more use, and higher education was linked to better financial and technical capacity, so peri-urban systems were better managed. Regression and ratio estimates, no legal or institutional exposure tested.
fields.section: Full text: Abstract; Materials and methods (household survey, participatory meetings); Results; Discussion

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a household survey of about 1,000 households in four rural and four peri-urban water supply systems in Valle del Cauca, Colombia found low ratios of perceived use to water supplied in most rural systems and lower perceived use than in peri-urban systems, with household size, education, age and occupation as drivers; read in full text 2026-10-04.
